raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation When deploying Kimi K3 on H100 GPU with EP64/TP32/DP2, the post-attention path performs AR -> RS -> AG before entering MoE. The RS is redundant because the attention outputs are already replicated within each attention-TP group. ## Modifications - Add attention-DP process groups that connect matching attention-TP ranks. - For replicated inputs with CP=1, replace RS32 + AG64 with a direct AG2 across the attention-DP group. - Keep the existing path as the fallback for other configurations. - Add a unit test for attention-DP group construction. ### Communication Flow Consider a smaller configuration with four ranks, attention TP2, DP2, and CP1. `A` and `B` are the complete local token tensors from the two DP replicas; `A0/A1` and `B0/B1` are their TP shards. **Before: RS2 + AG4** ```mermaid flowchart LR A0["DP0 after attention AR
r0 = A, r1 = A"] B0["DP1 after attention AR
r2 = B, r3 = B"] A1["Keep one replica
r0 = A, r1 = 0"] B1["Keep one replica
r2 = B, r3 = 0"] A2["RS2
r0 = A0, r1 = A1"] B2["RS2
r2 = B0, r3 = B1"] G["AG4 across r0-r3"] O["Every rank
[A0, A1, B0, B1] = [A, B]"] A0 --> A1 --> A2 --> G B0 --> B1 --> B2 --> G G --> O ``` The old path splits tensors that are already replicated, then gathers the shards back together across the full TP group. **After: direct AG2** ```mermaid flowchart LR A["After attention AR
r0 = A, r1 = A
r2 = B, r3 = B"] G0["attention-DP group for TP rank 0
{r0 = A, r2 = B}
AG2"] G1["attention-DP group for TP rank 1
{r1 = A, r3 = B}
AG2"] O0["r0, r2 = [A, B]"] O1["r1, r3 = [A, B]"] A --> G0 --> O0 A --> G1 --> O1 ``` Both paths produce the same `[A, B]` tensor on every rank. The new path avoids reduce-scatter and uses a smaller DP-only all-gather group. ## Accuracy Tests This is a communication-only optimization and does not change model computation. But feel free to ask if that's necessary. ## Speed Tests and Profiling On Kimi K3 with H100 EP64/TP32/DP2, this change improves performance by approximately 20%. Torch profiler traces before and after the optimization will be added below to show the reduction in communication kernels. **Before** **After** ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #30813936106](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30813936106) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #30813935863](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30813935863)

`bench_serving.py` -> `benchmark/serving.py`, `test/srt/` -> `test/registered/`.

## Pull request overview This PR optimizes Kimi K3’s post-attention communication path for mixed TP+EP deployments by introducing attention-DP process groups and using them to avoid redundant reduce-scatter + all-gather sequences when inputs are already replicated within attention-TP groups. **Changes:** - Add construction/lifecycle management for a new `attention_dp` process group in `parallel_state.initialize_model_parallel()`. - Introduce a fast-path in `dp_attention._dp_gather_via_all_gather()` to perform a direct all-gather over the attention-DP group when `CP==1`. - Add a unit test verifying `attention_dp` group rank construction. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 2 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | `test/registered/unit/distributed/test_parallel_state.py` | Adds a unit test to validate `attention_dp` group construction for a TP8 / attn-DP2 configuration. | | `python/sglang/srt/layers/dp_attention.py` | Adds a new fast-path gather that uses the attention-DP group to eliminate redundant comms when inputs are replicated and `CP==1`. | | `python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py` | Adds `_ATTN_DP`, `get_attn_dp_group()`, initializes `attention_dp` groups, and destroys them during teardown. | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

The new fast-path calls get_attn_dp_group() whenever CP==1, but _ATTN_DP is only initialized when attention_data_parallel_size > 1. For the common case attention_data_parallel_size==1 (default) with attn TP > 1, this branch will assert and crash during dp_gather_replicate(). Gate the optimization on attention-DP actually being enabled (e.g., by checking that attention TP size differs from full TP size).

nodes.body: initialize_model_parallel() now uses attention_data_parallel_size to compute attn_tp_size, but there are still no parameter validations for attention_data_parallel_size/attention_context_model_parallel_size. Passing 0 (or a combination that doesn't divide tensor_model_parallel_size) will currently produce a ZeroDivisionError or silently construct incorrect groups. Consider adding explicit >=1 and divisibility checks alongside the existing decode_context_parallel_size validation, so misconfigurations fail fast with a clear error.
